title: The Man Who Mailed Himself Home
sources: BBC News, 'The man who mailed himself out of London in a box' (1964; Reg Spiers was stranded in London, built a 5x3x2.5 ft crate labelled paint, and shipped himself air cargo cash-on-delivery to Perth)
National Archives of Australia: cargo manifests and records of Reg Spiers shipment from London to Western Australia in October 1964

lines.text: In nineteen sixty-four, an athlete mailed himself home in a wooden box.
lines.caps: In 1964, | an athlete | mailed himself | home | in a wooden box.

lines.text: Just to avoid paying for a plane ticket.
See, Reg was stranded in London with zero dollars,
and a flight back home cost three hundred pounds,
lines.caps: and a flight | back home | cost 300 pounds,

lines.text: So he built a five foot wooden crate,
lines.caps: So he built | a 5-foot | wooden crate,

lines.text: and climbed inside with some canned food and a pillow.
He shipped the box cash on delivery,
meaning he didn't have to pay a single dime upfront.
mostly upside down in freezing cargo holds.
When the crate finally touched down in Australia,
Reg waited for the handlers to walk away,
and casually strolled right out of the airport.
